plugins.name: astra-methodology
plugins.description: ASTRA methodology plugin with coding convention enforcement, data standard, international code standards, naming validation, quality gates, Slack integration, service manual auto-generator, UX/UI/Dev/QA Screen-ID based handoff package generator, role-based persona agents, and /autorun self-improving full pipeline. v5.12.0 NEW: /uat-parallel skill â Playwright-powered parallel sibling of /user-test. Reuses 100% of docs/tests/uat-cases/*.md format and the /user-test HTML report template (same docs/tests/uat-reports/{SESSION_ID}/ layout with index.html, issues.md, session.json, screenshots/). Each worker holds an isolated BrowserContext (separate cookies / localStorage / sessionStorage) so multi-user flows and race conditions do not collide; per-step hard timeout (UAT_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS, default 30s) + per-case timeout (UAT_CASE_TIMEOUT_MS, default 300s) kill stuck cases without blocking other workers. Bootstraps @playwright/test + chromium on first run via a single AskUserQuestion HITL (~150 MB). Args: --workers N (default min(4, cpu/2)) / --from / --priority / --feature / --timeout / --headed / --browser chromium|firefox|webkit. No interactive mode â auto-batch only. Runtime artifacts copied idempotently into .astra/uat/ (uat-runner.spec.ts + playwright.config.ts) on every invocation. Severity assignment in the runner mirrors user-test/references/assertion-guide.md Â§3 (CRITICAL 5xx / Uncaught; HIGH 4xx primary + 401/403 + no URL change; MEDIUM missing CTA + text mismatch; LOW default). Failed cases yield Playwright trace .zip archives at traces/{UAT-ID}.zip â replayable via `npx playwright show-trace ...` for DOM/network/console timeline debugging that Chrome MCP cannot produce. Solves the two main /user-test limits: sequential single-page execution doesn't scale beyond a few cases, and a stuck case blocks the rest of the run. References progressive-disclosure into parallel-guide.md (worker tuning, isolation guarantees, debugging flaky cases, CI integration sketch). v5.11.2 NEW: /pr-merge Step 8.4.5.1 (post-merge promotion-path prompt â dev / staging / skip) now always fires AskUserQuestion, even under --auto. Previously --auto silently picked dev; the merge target branch where the integration branch finally lands is a deployment-surface decision with no safe unattended default. /autorun and /sprint-init --auto now treat this as a routine HITL pause â pipeline still completes end-to-end in a single invocation but the user picks the target. Direct integration â main is intentionally NOT offered here (the explicit /pr-merge --main promotion, with version bump + release checks, remains the only production path). All other --auto behaviors (commit confirmation, final-merge approval, Step 4.5 integration auto-pick, Step 4.5.4 base auto-pick, Step 10.0 promotion-source defaults) are unchanged. v5.11.1 NEW: integration-branch model extended to --staging and --main promotion modes. New Step 10.0 asks the promotion source â legacy bulk (dev for --staging, staging for --main) OR a specific integration branch (feat/<name>/fix/<name>) from top-3 most-recent â so urgent hotfixes can land ONLY that feature on staging or directly on main without dragging other staging changes. Integration-source promotions skip Step 8 code review (already passed on source sprint PRs); bulk sources keep the review loop. Step 10.1 PR body varies by source type for traceability. Under --auto: --staging defaults to dev, --main defaults to staging (legacy paths preserved). v5.11.0 NEW: integration-branch model for /pr-merge â sprint PRs no longer target dev directly. The new Step 4.5 picks a feature- or fix-level integration branch (feat/<name> or fix/<name>) interactively: pick from top 3 existing branches by recent activity, or create new with user-chosen base (default origin/dev; options include origin/staging, origin/main, origin/master, custom). Classification (feat vs fix) and slug auto-inferred from Conventional Commit prefixes on the sprint branch, sprint-slug keywords, and blueprint Â§1+Â§10 keyword scan. After sprint PR merges into the integration branch, the new Step 8.4.5 asks the promotion path: 'dev (standard, default)' / 'staging (fast hotfix)' / 'skip' â a promotion PR is created and merged without fresh code review (sprint PR already passed). Integration branches are PERSISTENT â Step 9 explicit guard prevents auto-deletion; only feat/sprint-* and fix/sprint-* are eligible for git branch -d. Step 3.5 query updated to filter PRs by head~feat/sprint-* AND base~^(feat|fix)/ with backward-compat fallback to base=dev. /sprint-init Step 1.5 also became interactive â the sprint source branch is user-chosen (default dev; options staging/main/master/custom); passed through to astra_create_sprint_worktree. Under --auto: integration-branch selection reuses existing-name-matching else creates new from dev; promotion = dev; sprint source = dev â /autorun and /sprint-init --auto still complete end-to-end. Multiple-pending-PR detection preserves AskUserQuestion HITL even under --auto. Promotion modes (--staging, --main) and stagingâdev cascade unaffected. Trade-off: one sprint = up to 2 PRs (sprintâintegration, integrationâtarget). Benefit: feature- or bugfix-level promotion granularity â urgent hotfixes land on staging directly without queuing through dev. v5.10.0 NEW: /blueprint worktree-first order â Step 1.5 enforces branch/location guards (non-standard branch aborts with error; already in sprint worktree â reused for secondary blueprints), Step 1.6 delegates to /sprint-init --scaffold-only to create the sprint worktree first, Step 1.7 cd's into it, and Steps 2-6 author + review + commit the blueprint *inside* the sprint worktree on the sprint branch (no dev commit). /sprint-init --scaffold-only is a new flag that (a) suppresses prompt-map Feature 1.1 (blueprint authoring) and renumbers remaining steps as 1.1=DB Design, 1.2=Test Cases, 1.3=Implementation (new Variant B), (b) is incompatible with --auto (no blueprint to drive auto pipeline), and (c) exits cleanly after Step 4 so the calling /blueprint owns the consolidated output. The legacy --from-blueprint flag is preserved as a backward-compat alias. /autorun Stage 3 unchanged in behavior since /blueprint now does the worktree creation; Stage 4 (/sprint-init re-entry) is an idempotent no-op in the standard path. commands/blueprint.md description + behavior summary table updated. CLAUDE.md Worktree Isolation section + Skill Catalog row + Recommended Workflow updated. Removes the v5.8/5.9 cross-branch dev-visibility commit logic â simpler invariants. v5.9.0 NEW: /user-test skill â AI-assisted UAT (User Acceptance Testing) for end-user flows. Drives Chrome MCP with hard-assertion verification (URL / Network / DOM / Console) and auto-assigns severity (CRITICAL / HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW) per a fixed rule table. Two modes: interactive (URL + Vietnamese natural-language flow description, generates draft test case and offers to save) and --auto (batch-runs pre-authored test cases under docs/tests/uat-cases/, filterable by --priority / --feature / --from). Output: timestamped session folder docs/tests/uat-reports/{YYYY-MM-DD-HHmm}/ with index.html (visual report + per-step thumbnails), issues.md (only when failures exist), session.json. On FAIL the case is skipped and the next case continues. Progressive disclosure into references/assertion-guide.md and assets/report-template.html. Distinct from /test-run (developer-authored technical integration tests) and /test-scenario (scenario authoring). Runtime output language follows /select-language; default Vietnamese. No GitHub Issue integration â local issues.md only. Also v5.9.0: /pr-merge two-phase policy. `gh pr merge` only runs from the main worktree. Sprint Phase (invoked inside a sprint worktree) handles commit â push â PR â review â fix loop and stops; the user `cd`s to the main worktree and re-invokes `/pr-merge`, which auto-detects the pending sprint PR (base=dev, head=feat/sprint-*) via Step 3.5 and finalizes the merge + worktree removal via Step M1. Step 8.5 (SprintâMain handoff) and Step 8.3 (phase decision based on STARTED_FROM_SPRINT flag) are new. Under `--auto`, the skill itself `cd`s to the main worktree and continues into Main Phase so /autorun and /sprint-init --auto still complete end-to-end in one invocation. Multiple-pending-PR detection preserves AskUserQuestion even under --auto. Promotion modes (--staging, --main) are unaffected. v5.8.0 NEW: /blueprint Step 6.5 auto-creates the sprint worktree by delegating to /sprint-init at the end of authoring â the skill does NOT change the user's cwd (to avoid relying on unreliable Skill-to-Skill cwd propagation), and Step 7 output shows the user a concrete `cd .astra-worktrees/sprint-<N>-<slug>/` command to run next so they can enter the worktree explicitly.
